question: During the late 17th century, the actions of English pirates like Henry Every (who captured the royal pilgrim ship Ganj-i-Sawai) severely strained relations between the EIC and Mughal officials. Which of the following was the immediate Mughal response to this event?
options: The Mughals banned all European trading companies from entering Indian waters.
The Governor of Surat imprisoned EIC officers, and Aurangzeb ordered a complete blockade of Bombay.
Aurangzeb hired Dutch naval commanders to protect Mughal ships.
The Mughals immediately executed all English merchants in Bengal.
explanation: Henry Every's capture of the Ganj-i-Sawai (1695), which was carrying immense wealth and Haj pilgrims (including members of the Mughal royal family), infuriated Aurangzeb. The Governor of Surat imprisoned the EIC president and other staff. Aurangzeb put a trade ban and ordered the siege of Bombay and other factories until the EIC agreed to compensate and patrol the seas against piracy.
